description: FAME provides common scheduling, communication and input-output components for agent-based energy-system simulations. Its Java core works with Python input-output tools, portable binary formats and optional parallel execution. The provider is FAME project / DLR. Coverage: The framework is generic to user-defined models, from laptop runs to computing clusters. Spatial units, time steps and study periods are defined by the application. Access: The GitLab wiki was read through its public API after the HTML page returned only a shell. No software or simulation files were obtained. Licence and cost: The provider wiki states that all FAME components are open source. Exact component-specific licences were not read. Limitations: Core and I/O testing claims are provider statements. Scientific validity still depends on each model’s agents and parameterisation. For simulation it supports the construction and parallel execution of energy-market agent models. Related resources: Related record model-amiris describes an electricity-market application that runs on FAME.
